newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lower oil costs keep S.African PPI in check in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Lower oil costs keep S.African PPI in check in Nov.

text.p: A decrease in the cost of crude petroleum imports in November contributed to a slightly lower than expected South African producer price inflation in November, according to the Central Statistical Service.
November PPI rose 0.5 percent in November from October and 8.5 percent year-on-year, against the consensus forecast of economists for increases of 0.7 and 8.7 respectively.
PPI stood at 1.3 percent month-on-month and 8.3 year-on-year in October.
The import price of crude petroleum showed a monthly decrease of 6.6 percent, a decline which the CSS put down to the arrival of several large consignments at good prices.

Economists have in recent months questioned the reliability of the imported oil compannent in producer price data but CSS head Mark Orkin said the figures -- supplied by Customs and Excise -- inevitably fluctuated depending on consignment size.

"In months where the total imported volume is large, there are large consignments obtained at favourable prices, which bring down the average unit price," he said in a special statement accompanying the November PPI data.
"Conversely, in months where the total volume is small, and made up of small consignments, the unit prices of such consignments are evidently disadvantageous, sharply raising the average unit price."

The fall in the oil price helped keep the imported component of PPI to a monthly increase of just 0.1 percent, despite the weak rand. Imported manufactured products (with a 90 percent weighting) increased 0.8 percent, but this was counteracted by the 6.6 percent drop in the cost of oil (with a 6.7 percent weighting).
Locally-produced commodities rose a larger 0.5 percent month-on-month, with relatively large increases recorded in several areas, including agricultural products, fish and food at manufacturing.

Bond dealers said the PPI data was mildly encouraging, helping yields on the benchmark R150 government stock edge down to around 15.97 percent from 16.01 immediately before the data was released at 0900 GMT.
